cohort: Teenage pregnancies managed between January 2013 and December 2017 at the Benue State University Teaching Hospital, Makurdi, North-Central, Nigeria.
finding: Teenage births had an incidence of 2.06% and were associated with obstetric risks and adverse pregnancy outcomes including malaria, anemia, hypertension, increased need for labor augmentation/induction, cesarean section, and perinatal mortality.
